events.title: First Human Heart Transplant
events.description: Surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the world's first human-to-human heart transplant at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town, South Africa, on patient Louis Washkansky, who lived for 18 days after the operation.
events.significance: This milestone opened the era of modern transplant surgery and led to major advances in immunosuppression and organ donation, saving countless lives in the decades since.

events.title: Illinois Admitted as the 21st U.S. State
events.description: Illinois was admitted to the Union as the 21st state, following the passage of an enabling act and the approval of its constitution by Congress.
events.significance: Illinois became a major center of agriculture, transportation, and industry, and later produced figures such as Abraham Lincoln who shaped the nation's history.

events.title: Bhopal Gas Tragedy
events.description: A leak of methyl isocyanate gas from the Union Carbide pesticide plant in Bhopal, India, exposed hundreds of thousands of people to toxic fumes overnight, killing thousands immediately and many more in later years.
events.significance: It is considered one of the worst industrial disasters in history and prompted worldwide reforms in industrial safety, environmental regulation, and corporate accountability.

events.title: First SMS Text Message Sent
events.description: Engineer Neil Papworth sent the first text message, reading 'Merry Christmas,' over the Vodafone network in the United Kingdom to Richard Jarvis, who received it on a computer.
events.significance: The event marked the beginning of text messaging, which grew into a dominant form of global communication and paved the way for modern mobile messaging.

events.title: Death of Robert Louis Stevenson
events.description: Scottish novelist and poet Robert Louis Stevenson, author of Treasure Island and Strange Case of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde, died in Samoa at age 44 after suffering a cerebral hemorrhage.
events.significance: Stevenson's adventure stories and psychological fiction remain widely read and have profoundly influenced popular literature and storytelling.
